method.opening: Four seconds from each opening scene, using a fresh browser context and the 35 numbered tab routes. Guarded views were played for the survey. Initial rendering, specific secondary modes, custom palettes and arbitrary interactions can differ.
method.screen: All 35 scans at 1024 × 768 cover visible canvases sampled on a four-CSS-pixel grid. The scan uses fixed positions at 60 callbacks per modeled second. Stretch runs on its own native clock. The phone screen uses 390 × 844. Primary simulations use the same seeded random generator for controlled comparisons.
method.recurringFineDetail: For a sampled point, accumulate rises and falls of at least 0.10 in linear relative luminance with the darker state below 0.80. Pair alternating changes into nonoverlapping cycles. Mark a point when a rolling second contains four completed cycles. Slide an approximately 341 × 256 CSS-pixel window over the screen and record its highest percentage of marked points. Different points can qualify at different times. This is a repeat footprint, not simultaneous flash area.
method.spatialAverage: Apply the same rise/fall detector to mean luminance in fixed 32 × 32 CSS-pixel blocks. Report blocks with two or more full cycles in the entire four-second run. This catches slower broad pulsing that may never reach four cycles in a second.
method.red: Also screen adjacent sampled frames for alternating transitions involving saturated red and a chromaticity difference above 0.2 in CIE u′v′. Screened defaults produced no four-cycle red footprint. The screen covers a subset of possible red transitions.
method.visiblePage: The seven desktop and six phone follow-ups use composited Chrome screenshots, including text and overlapping controls. They sample at 30 fps while the simulation advances at 60 callbacks/s. Three desktop follow-ups also use 60 screenshots/s. Disk v2 was repeated on a phone with its controls hidden. The per-tab 60 fps canvas screen can include canvas pixels under a panel.
method.scope: These are project-specific design checks. They cover one browser and short opening states. The measured footprint and broad-pulse measures do not establish WCAG conformance or a medical safety classification.
